action_summary: The repository's semiring Why-Provenance JTMS memory (Move 3 of unified_unfamiliar_leapfrog_v1) answers two of the six operations the MEME protocol asks for -- multi-hop cascade retraction that preserves diamond alternative proofs, and absence for a fact that was established and lost its support. Measured on main before this PR, three operations have no API at all: aggregation, tracking (entity renames), and absence for a rule that never fired. This PR adds them by composition, not duplication: the fact store, the polynomials and the cascade stay in the existing engine, and canonical/swe_kernel/meme_protocol_memory_v1.py adds a ground rule layer that saturates incrementally, Z-set aggregates that distinguish a member the operator deleted (the smaller total is the intended answer) from a member that lost its support upstream (the total is now unsupported and must be refused, naming the member), rename tracking that carries derived facts and poisons the stale name, and a rule-blocked absence answer that names the rule and the missing body. The new six-operation bench canonical/evaluation/meme_protocol_bench_v1.py scores the subsystem against a from-scratch fixpoint oracle with a no-dependency-edges baseline, a liar control and a stub control.

The protocol bench is this repository's instrument, judged by this repository's oracle; the baseline is our own no-edges implementation, not a measurement of anyone else's system.
